question: The captain stood at the ship's ____.
solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. stern .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"stern"** refers to the back part of a ship, which is where the captain often stands to oversee navigation and operations.
 
• Option 1 **"stair"** refers to steps and is unrelated to the parts of a ship.
 
• Option 2 **"steer"** refers to the act of directing or controlling the ship, but it is not a location or part of the ship.
 
• Option 4 **"stow"** refers to the act of packing or storing items, and it is not a location on the ship.

Correct sentence: *The captain stood at the ship's **stern**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parts of a Ship:**

 
 
• **Stern:** The rear part of the ship.
 
• **Bow:** The front part of the ship.
 
• **Deck:** The main horizontal platform on the ship.
 
• **Hull:** The body of the ship.
 
 
 
• **Nautical Terminology:**
 
 
• **Port:** The left-hand side of the ship when facing forward.
 
• **Starboard:** The right-hand side of the ship when facing forward.
